_meta.question: which descriptor fields cannot do what their name promises
_meta.note: A1 advisories are NOT presented as defects: a 4-bit dst nibble is a real AGX compact-form encoding. They are the places where the descriptor caps an operand and the normative doc must say so explicitly.

decisive_defects.label: hardware-run
decisive_defects.detail: descriptor declares 8 bits but only 7 are choosable (128 legal values); the rest are pinned by its own match, so the field is narrower than it says and any sweep through it under-covers

decisive_defects.label: hardware-run
decisive_defects.detail: descriptor declares 8 bits but only 4 are choosable (16 legal values); the rest are pinned by its own match, so the field is narrower than it says and any sweep through it under-covers

decisive_defects.label: hardware-run
decisive_defects.detail: every bit of the span is pinned by this descriptor's own match: exactly ONE legal value, so the field cannot name an operand

advisories.label: hardware-run
advisories.detail: 4 free bits and NO sibling extension field in this descriptor, so the operand is capped at r0..r15. May be a true hardware limit; the doc must say which.
